non_blocking_notes.text: The git replace object route is deliberate and detectable. If the committed code blob is replaced (git replace <orig> <evil>) and the file is marked skip-worktree before make_freeze, then git status is clean, `git show HEAD:` returns the evil bytes, and `git diff <cand> HEAD` is unchanged. make_freeze binds the evil hash, ready passes and execute runs the edited code under a FREEZE that names the genuine candidate and review (demonstrated on a synthetic copy). A fresh clone of the freeze commit refuses with bound file drift, and the FREEZE's bound hash differs from the candidate blob. Recommended for a future candidate: run git with --no-replace-objects (GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1), and refuse lowercase or S index flags. For this lineage, the final adjudicator must re-run the freeze verification in a fresh clone and check every bound hash in FREEZE.json against `git show <candidate>:<path>`.

The code cannot know which candidate was actually reviewed. A forged review naming a different, edited commit passes make_freeze and ready. The final adjudicator must check that FREEZE.qualified_candidate_commit == 93d82c87d2f5aa33109f5b37125caf283967b694, and that the bound review files are byte-identical to the QUALIFICATION_REVIEW.json/.md delivered by this reviewer.

Untested layers in the r5 checks. 17 of the 20 reviewer mutants survived (see 2c); none is unsound under the runbook. Suggested tests for a future revision: a well-formed extra or misnamed file in the review dir; two review dirs; a qualification_rNx suffix; a review candidate given as a prefix or an empty string; a verdict such as QUALIFICATION_NOT_ACCEPTED; a merge freeze commit whose first parent is the candidate; the guard under -s and -E -s; make_freeze with a GATE or SPEC edit under assume-unchanged.

Stop conditions: define whether a new freeze of the same candidate is permitted after a lineage ends. Recommended: none after any reservation exists; before that, only for a refusal that read no source. Also allow a plain retry for invocation errors that refuse before any check (missing -I, wrong subcommand or path).
